Requirement: The system shall accept applications with display name, email, research interests, preferred language, and optional affiliation/biography.
Acceptance criterion: Required fields validate; optional academic affiliation is not a mandatory credential; applicant receives a reference/status page.

Requirement: The system shall verify email ownership before an application enters the approval queue.
Acceptance criterion: Expired/used verification links fail safely; repeated requests are rate-limited; an unverified applicant cannot create projects.

Requirement: Administrators shall approve, reject with a reason, or request more information; every decision is attributed and dated.
Acceptance criterion: Pending/rejected accounts cannot call researcher APIs; approval enables the same account without recreating it.

Requirement: The system shall support secure login, logout, session expiry, password recovery, and session revocation.
Acceptance criterion: Recovery does not reveal whether an email is registered; revoked sessions fail on the next protected request.

Requirement: Approved accounts shall have personal home, library, owned/shared projects, notification preferences, and downloads.
Acceptance criterion: Two accounts see their own data; owning one project imposes no one-project limitation.

Requirement: Researchers shall control public profile fields independently of private account data.
Acceptance criterion: Email is private by default; opting into a public profile exposes only selected fields and public research.

Requirement: Administrators shall suspend/reactivate access with an audit reason; researchers may request account closure.
Acceptance criterion: Suspension blocks new writes/shares/downloads; data is retained for resolution; closure handles owned projects and existing publications explicitly.

Requirement: Administrative and editorial accounts shall use multi-factor authentication (TOTP with single-use recovery codes in R1a; other methods later); researchers shall be offered it.
Acceptance criterion: A privileged action requires a fully authenticated session; recovery events are audited.

Requirement: Administration shall manage application queues, approval reasons, suspensions, platform roles, and appeal/contact requests.
Acceptance criterion: Role changes are audited; editors cannot grant themselves administrator powers.

Requirement: Authorized staff shall manage application and invitation rate limits, abuse reports, upload/export quotas, allowed file types, job failures, rights flags, and public-content reports.
Acceptance criterion: Policy changes do not silently destroy research; affected users receive an actionable explanation.

Requirement: Support access to private content shall be explicitly granted for a scope and duration, with reason and audit.
Acceptance criterion: Ordinary admin searches do not reveal private evidence; expired support grants fail.

Requirement: Deletions, transfers, submissions, decisions, releases, rights changes, exports, and privileged actions shall be audited.
Acceptance criterion: Audit entries identify actor/action/object/time/outcome and cannot be edited through normal research UI.

Requirement: Operational dashboards shall monitor indexing, queue latency, errors, storage, backup results, and export completeness.
Acceptance criterion: Operators can detect failed jobs without reading private research content unnecessarily.

Requirement: Researchers shall open a saved side-by-side comparison of selected source occurrences with source headers and annotation links.
Acceptance criterion: Original wording is visible; lacking occurrence-specific wording produces a limitation notice rather than invented variants.

Requirement: Researchers shall compare selected chains as readable ordered lists with narrator and formula inspection.
Acceptance criterion: Unresolved ordering is displayed as uncertain; narrator clicks open the correct identity or ambiguity record.

Requirement: A narrator dossier shall combine identity fields, available teachers/students, related reports, and attributed criticism.
Acceptance criterion: Every assessment links to its available source; missing information is labelled unknown.

Requirement: A criticism comparison shall filter by target narrator, critic, expression, book, and recorded category while preserving exact qawl text.
Acceptance criterion: Different critics' wording is not replaced by a single numerical score; normalized labels remain separate.

Requirement: Analyses shall save their input IDs/versions, settings, creator, time, annotations, and output version.
Acceptance criterion: Reopening restores the selected inputs; rerunning against changed data creates a new analysis version.

Requirement: Researchers shall create evidence from an exact source span or record, retaining original text, locator, source version/snapshot, collector, and timestamp.
Acceptance criterion: A citation opens the precise selected source where available; missing volume/page is labelled incomplete.

Requirement: Evidence shall support candidate, included, reviewed, excluded, and unresolved states, with reasons for exclusion and unresolved status.
Acceptance criterion: State changes are attributed; reviewed does not imply authentic, correct, or agreed.

Requirement: Annotations shall distinguish source quotation, personal interpretation, attributed scholarly judgment, and machine suggestion.
Acceptance criterion: Export and public preview preserve these labels; unaccepted machine text cannot appear as an attributed scholar statement.

Requirement: Annotations shall support private-to-author or project-shared visibility, with explicit promotion from private to shared.
Acceptance criterion: Owners and publication reviewers cannot read another author's private annotations through exports, search, or document links.

Requirement: Evidence shall link to findings as supporting, opposing, contextual, or unresolved evidence.
Acceptance criterion: One item can support several findings without duplicating its source; opposite interpretations remain possible.

Requirement: Deleting or changing referenced evidence shall report dependencies and preserve prior document/submission versions.
Acceptance criterion: A user is warned before removing a used link; a published citation does not silently change its quoted content.

Requirement: Researchers shall propose corpus corrections with the current value, proposed value, evidence, and explanation.
Acceptance criterion: Proposal enters a separate corpus-editor queue; acceptance in a research project does not update canonical data.

Requirement: Researchers shall download a document, selected resources, an entire project, or all currently authorized research across their account.
Acceptance criterion: Account-wide export supports multiple projects; scope preview shows personal and shared material separately.

Requirement: Complete project exports shall include metadata, resources, saved queries/runs/result sets, evidence, analyses, tasks/discussions, findings/documents, citations, eligible revision histories, research activity, and permitted attachments.
Acceptance criterion: Private-to-other-user content is excluded; the manifest enumerates included objects and explains unavailable/omitted files.

Requirement: Account-wide export shall include personal library/notes and each selected authorized project's shared research plus the requester's applicable private annotations.
Acceptance criterion: It does not include other members' personal libraries, private notes, credentials, or operational security logs.

Requirement: Exports shall offer human-readable HTML/Markdown, Unicode JSON, CSV for tabular data, BibTeX/RIS references, PDF for selected documents, and ZIP packages.
Acceptance criterion: A package opens offline with a local index; Arabic/Sorani render in PDF; references retain stable IDs.

Requirement: Large exports shall be resumable background jobs with queued/running/complete/partial/failed/cancelled/expired states.
Acceptance criterion: Closing the browser does not cancel a job; retries do not create conflicting duplicate packages; partial output is never labelled complete.

Requirement: Every export shall record requester, scope, content versions, corpus identity where available, generation time, format/schema version, counts, exclusions, and checksums for files.
Acceptance criterion: Users can verify package contents and distinguish a missing eligible file from an intentionally excluded restricted item.

Requirement: Authorization and rights shall be checked at request, generation, and download; download links shall be authenticated and expire.
Acceptance criterion: Revocation before retrieval prevents download of affected private material; jobs are rebuilt or cancelled when their authorized scope changes.

Requirement: Export limits shall partition eligible material into linked packages rather than silently truncating “all research.”
Acceptance criterion: A large export yields a complete manifest across numbered parts or an explicit failure with retry options.

Requirement: Researchers shall be able to regenerate expired downloads, see storage/quota limits, and retry failures.
Acceptance criterion: Seven-day expiry applies to generated packages, not the underlying research; regeneration rechecks current access.

Requirement: Researchers shall save books, chapters, sections, reports, occurrences, chains, narrators, judgments, and source passages from the corpus.
Acceptance criterion: Save/open preserves exact object type and ID; a report occurrence is distinguishable from a report-level record.

Requirement: My Library shall support named collections, tags, favourites, personal notes, search, and filtering by type/source/date.
Acceptance criterion: An item may appear in multiple collections without duplicating the canonical record.

Requirement: Researchers shall add an external bibliographical reference with URL or identifiers, author, title, date where known, and access date.
Acceptance criterion: An incomplete citation is permitted and visibly flagged; unknown metadata is not fabricated.

Requirement: Researchers shall add a personal item to one or more projects with an explicit preview of shared content.
Acceptance criterion: Private notes are unchecked by default; a collaborator sees only the selected shared content.

Requirement: Project resources shall have project-local tags, inclusion rationale, and collection membership independent of My Library.
Acceptance criterion: Changing a project tag does not rename a personal tag or modify another project's association.

Requirement: Duplicate additions shall identify an existing association while allowing distinct excerpts from the same source.
Acceptance criterion: Saving the same book twice prompts reuse; saving two different page passages produces two identifiable excerpts.

Requirement: Source unavailability or changes shall not silently destroy saved research references.
Acceptance criterion: A deleted/merged/changed corpus target shows a status and preserved permitted snapshot; the original saved locator remains visible.

Requirement: Removing a library association shall not delete its source or another project's resource.
Acceptance criterion: Removing a personal favourite leaves previously shared project evidence intact.

Requirement: Approved researchers shall create multiple projects, each with a unique ID, title, question, scope, language, owner, and private workspace.
Acceptance criterion: Creating Project B neither changes Project A nor shares its resources or members.

Requirement: The project index shall distinguish owned/shared projects and filter by stage, tag, title, archived state, and recent activity.
Acceptance criterion: A membership invitation does not show the workspace until accepted; a removed project disappears from the former member's list.

Requirement: Every project shall contain independently scoped resources, queries, evidence, analyses, tasks, discussions, findings, documents, and publication records.
Acceptance criterion: Direct API requests cannot use an authorized project ID to retrieve an item belonging to a different project.

Requirement: Projects shall use explicit stages: scoping, collecting, analysing, writing, reviewing, completed. Archived state shall be separate.
Acceptance criterion: Owners can move backwards with an activity entry; archiving an unfinished project does not mark it completed.

Requirement: Project overview shall expose scope, milestones, evidence counts by state, open questions, and next actions.
Acceptance criterion: Numerical progress identifies its denominator or manual-estimate basis.

Requirement: Authorized researchers shall copy selected resources, queries, and analyses into another project with provenance and a visibility preview.
Acceptance criterion: Membership, private comments, and publication authority are not copied; changes in the destination do not mutate the source project.

Requirement: Owners shall transfer ownership (available from R1b, when memberships exist), archive/unarchive, or soft-delete/restore a project.
Acceptance criterion: Transfer requires acceptance; a trashed project is read-only during recovery and does not silently remove a public publication.

Requirement: Search shall support original-text exact phrase and normalized lexical modes with mode visibly identified.
Acceptance criterion: Exact and normalized results can differ; highlights point to the original text; original Arabic/Sorani wording is never overwritten.

Requirement: Search shall support typed filters for book/author/chapter/section, report type, narrator, known chain relationship, critic, recorded hukm, and available dates.
Acceptance criterion: Unsupported or incomplete fields are labelled; unknown dates can be included explicitly rather than silently excluded.

Requirement: Results shall show type, source locator, relevant passage, available chain information, and why the item matched.
Acceptance criterion: Counts state whether they represent reports or occurrences; grouped results can expand to source occurrences.

Requirement: Researchers shall save a named query with text, filter structure, mode, sort, and personal/project scope.
Acceptance criterion: Reopening reconstructs the query; sharing a project query does not expose unrelated personal searches.

Requirement: Every saved-query execution shall record execution time, query-definition version, corpus/index identity, result count, and completion status.
Acceptance criterion: A partial/cancelled search is not labelled complete; rerunning creates a separate run record.

Requirement: Researchers shall preserve selected results or all results from a completed run as a result set with immutable membership.
Acceptance criterion: “All results” includes all matched pages at that run; limits/truncation are explicit and require a deliberate reduced selection.

Requirement: Result-set membership and saved evidence shall remain stable when the live corpus changes.
Acceptance criterion: A subsequent run can differ without silently adding/removing members of the earlier set.

Requirement: Researchers shall review selected results individually or in bulk and add them to project resources/evidence.
Acceptance criterion: Bulk operations return per-item outcomes, preserve provenance, and do not create unnoticed duplicates.

Requirement: All protected object access (read, write, search, preview, export, file retrieval, background job) shall pass through one policy module that evaluates the requester, project role, object visibility, and the object's actual project.
Acceptance criterion: A permission matrix generated from §3.2 and §12.1 runs as an automated test suite; no endpoint performs its own ad hoc role check.

Requirement: Findings shall contain a title/question, claim or conclusion, reasoning, supporting/opposing evidence, limitations, contributors, and status.
Acceptance criterion: A finding can be provisional or inconclusive; missing required public-submission fields are reported before submission.

Requirement: Projects shall support multiple documents and multiple findings, with many-to-many links between them.
Acceptance criterion: A main article and a chain summary are separate documents; editing one document creates a version, not another unrelated draft.

Requirement: The R1a editor shall be a structured Markdown editor with live preview supporting headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, quotations, footnotes/citations, per-block text direction for Arabic/Sorani/English, and autosave.
Acceptance criterion: Mixed-direction text and citations survive save/reload/export; last successful save and unsaved state are visible.

Requirement: Inserting evidence into writing shall create an explicit citation and retain original versus researcher-edited text.
Acceptance criterion: Paraphrase is not presented as an exact quotation; deleting a bibliography entry reports dependent citations.

Requirement: Documents shall support version history, comparison, and restoration without deleting subsequent history.
Acceptance criterion: Restoring an older version creates a new current version; attribution of earlier contributions remains. A stale save from a second session of the same user is rejected as a conflict.

Requirement: Citation generation shall use source metadata including work, edition, volume/page or stable alternative locator, and source-specific report number where available.
Acceptance criterion: Missing components are flagged; the system does not confuse source numbering with global report IDs.

Requirement: Owners shall draft and directly publish an announcement from a project without editorial preapproval.
Acceptance criterion: An approved researcher owning a project can publish a valid announcement; nonowners cannot.

Requirement: Announcements shall contain public title, question/summary, scope, research stage, keywords, credited participants who consent, and optional collaboration contact mechanism.
Acceptance criterion: Public preview excludes private notes, tasks, library items, email addresses, and workspace membership by default.

Requirement: Announcements shall be explicitly labelled as project announcements/ongoing research and not peer-reviewed findings.
Acceptance criterion: Public listings and detail pages show the type; announcement forms do not substitute for formal publication submission.

Requirement: Owners shall update or unpublish announcements, with retained internal history; administrators may moderate them with recorded reasons.
Acceptance criterion: Unpublishing removes public content from feeds/search; the private project survives; public caches are invalidated.

Requirement: Public announcements shall have stable URLs and optional links to later publications from the same project.
Acceptance criterion: A linked publication reveals only its released content; users cannot derive workspace access from the project URL.

Requirement: Owners shall invite approved accounts to project roles; invitations expire and require acceptance.
Acceptance criterion: Unapproved invitees complete approval first; an invitation alone reveals no private project evidence.

Requirement: Owners shall change/revoke roles; authorization shall apply immediately to subsequent requests and queued jobs.
Acceptance criterion: Removed users cannot read content through old URLs, cached API responses, or newly completed export links.

Requirement: Discussions shall attach to a project, evidence item, source span, analysis, finding, or document passage.
Acceptance criterion: Opening a comment reveals its target/context; private targets cannot notify unauthorized recipients.

Requirement: Tasks shall have title, assignee, context link, due date when used, and open/in-progress/blocked/done states.
Acceptance criterion: Only eligible members can be assigned; completing a task does not automatically resolve a scholarly disagreement.

Requirement: Notifications shall cover invitations, mentions, assignments, review decisions, and export completion with personal preferences.
Acceptance criterion: In-app notifications are available; email links require authorization and avoid including private passages.

Requirement: Shared edits shall retain author/time/version and prevent silent overwriting of concurrent changes.
Acceptance criterion: A stale editor is shown a conflict and can compare/recover their text; real-time simultaneous editing is not required for R1.

Requirement: Review threads shall allow resolved/unresolved states, reasons, and retained alternative interpretations.
Acceptance criterion: Resolving a thread preserves its history; project decisions identify who made them.

Requirement: Research activity shall be filterable by actor, object, and action without exposing private notes.
Acceptance criterion: Project members see relevant shared changes; security audit fields are restricted.

Requirement: Background jobs shall evaluate the requester's current permissions at execution and again before output release, not the permissions at enqueue time and not service credentials.
Acceptance criterion: AT-25 passes.

Requirement: Editors shall have queues by submission stage, assignee, age, and required action.
Acceptance criterion: A submission awaiting author revision is distinguishable from one awaiting a reviewer.

Requirement: Owners shall assemble a submission from selected findings/documents, authors, abstract, keywords, citations, eligible attachments, and a visibility/rights declaration.
Acceptance criterion: A preview lists every public component and every internal dependency needing resolution.

Requirement: Submission shall freeze an immutable package version while private research may continue separately.
Acceptance criterion: Editing the working document after submission does not change the editor's package.

Requirement: Editors shall triage submissions, request revisions, reject with a reason, or approve an exact package version.
Acceptance criterion: Only editor-authorized transitions succeed; the owner cannot approve their own submission merely through owner permissions.

Requirement: Editors shall assign at least one publication reviewer before approving formal findings under the default workflow.
Acceptance criterion: Reviewers access only the assigned package; a recorded review and editor decision identify the reviewed version.

Requirement: Conflict-of-interest declarations shall prevent authors from acting as the deciding editor/reviewer of their own submission.
Acceptance criterion: A conflicted editor must route the submission to another eligible editor; no eligible editor leaves it pending rather than bypassing review.

Requirement: Revision requests shall generate new submission versions with responses and preserved prior reviews.
Acceptance criterion: Approval of an earlier package cannot publish changed content from a later package.

Requirement: Approved packages shall publish only through an explicit editor release action.
Acceptance criterion: Approval alone leaves the item unpublished; release creates a stable public page, version, timestamp, and audit entry atomically.

Requirement: Public research pages shall show output type, title, abstract, authors, review-status label, content, citations, publication/version dates, limitations, and eligible downloads.
Acceptance criterion: Visitors can inspect permitted evidence without accessing private project discussions.

Requirement: Public research shall be discoverable by title, author, topic, type, language, and date, with separate announcement/results filters.
Acceptance criterion: Private or review-only material never appears in public search, suggestions, feeds, or metadata.

Requirement: Corrections and substantive revisions shall retain released versions and pass the relevant review workflow.
Acceptance criterion: Public corrections identify changes; released source quotations cannot be silently overwritten.

Requirement: Withdrawal/retraction shall preserve a public status notice and history except where a justified content-removal process requires removal.
Acceptance criterion: Visitors see current status; a withdrawn item is not displayed as an active approved finding.

Requirement: Author credit, source rights, and public licensing choices shall be confirmed before release.
Acceptance criterion: Unapproved participant names and restricted full-text files are blocked from publication; reference metadata can remain where permitted.

Requirement: The writer shall distinguish internal private/project links from publicly resolvable references before publication.
Acceptance criterion: A private evidence link blocks direct public exposure until a permitted public citation/excerpt is selected or the dependency is removed.

Requirement: Matn comparison shall offer alignment and addition/omission/substitution highlighting with adjustable normalization.
Acceptance criterion: Users can see unnormalized text and correct alignment; a difference is not automatically labelled a defect.

Requirement: Isnād analysis shall show shared nodes, branching, convergence, and formulas, with chain-list and graph views.
Acceptance criterion: Traversal is bounded; edge direction and selected sources remain visible; a graphic cannot invent missing intermediaries.

Requirement: The workbench shall support candidate Hadith-family grouping and shawāhid/mutābaʿāt collection with researcher-assigned relationship types.
Acceptance criterion: Algorithmic candidates and scholar-reviewed memberships remain separately labelled.

Requirement: An ʿilal case shall record competing chains/matns, discrepancy category, critics' statements, preferred versions, reasons, objections, and unresolved issues.
Acceptance criterion: A case can remain inconclusive; the system does not force an authenticity verdict.

Requirement: Temporal checks shall operate on supported date intervals and meeting/audition evidence.
Acceptance criterion: Impossible, possible, documented meeting, and documented audition are distinguishable; lifetime overlap is not treated as proof of hearing.

Requirement: Teacher-specific narrator assessment shall be representable where source evidence exists.
Acceptance criterion: A judgment about one teacher is not silently generalized to all transmissions by that narrator.

Requirement: Book-structure and terminology views shall expose chapters, occurrences, lexical concordances, and critic expressions with scoped counts.
Acceptance criterion: Counts identify coverage and unit; drill-down returns the contributing records.

Requirement: Visitors with verified accounts shall send collaboration-interest requests through a controlled form.
Acceptance criterion: Requests reveal only sender-selected details; acceptance is followed by explicit project invitation and approval checks.

Requirement: Researchers shall record structured historical assertions with alternatives, uncertainty, source, and adjudication.
Acceptance criterion: Estimated dates/identities remain distinguishable from attested statements and retain competing alternatives.

Requirement: Document exports shall additionally support editable DOCX, and structured analysis exports shall support documented graph/dataset formats.
Acceptance criterion: Citations and RTL paragraphs survive DOCX conversion; graph edges retain direction and provenance.

Requirement: The system shall support importing its documented research-package format into a new private project with preview.
Acceptance criterion: IDs are remapped, citations/provenance retained, and ownership, collaborators, public status, and approval decisions are not automatically recreated.

Requirement: Once the DATA-06 rights policy is approved, researchers shall upload permitted supporting files with type, size, ownership/rights statement, and description.
Acceptance criterion: Pending scans are inaccessible; unsupported files are rejected clearly; attachment metadata remains available after a failed upload for retry.

Requirement: Researchers shall import references from documented BibTeX/RIS formats with preview and duplicate handling.
Acceptance criterion: Invalid entries are reported individually; valid entries can be imported without silently overwriting existing references.

Requirement: Project creation shall offer takhrīj, narrator study, grading comparison, and ʿilal investigation templates.
Acceptance criterion: Each template provides editable questions, fields, and milestones; blank projects remain available.

Requirement: Approved datasets, annotated collections, and structured dossiers shall have type-specific public presentations and versioned downloads.
Acceptance criterion: A dataset identifies schema/version; a dossier retains source-linked evidence; neither is forced into an article-only layout.

Requirement: The system shall compare runs and show added/removed/changed results when stable identities permit.
Acceptance criterion: Changed records are distinguished from new records; missing historical coverage is reported.

Requirement: Researchers shall opt into scheduled reruns and notifications of relevant changes.
Acceptance criterion: Disabled schedules stop; notification recipients must still have access; repeated unchanged runs do not generate duplicate alerts.

Requirement: Findings shall support structured argument relationships, including objection, reply, qualification, and alternative conclusion.
Acceptance criterion: Users can inspect the original source behind a reasoning node and export the argument structure.

Requirement: Reproducible dataset outputs shall record selection rules, exclusions, labels, data dictionary, source snapshot, and version.
Acceptance criterion: A released dataset identifies included records and applicable redistribution conditions.

Requirement: The editor shall offer rich-text (WYSIWYG) editing of the same document model without altering stored citations or text direction.
Acceptance criterion: Documents round-trip between Markdown and rich-text modes without loss of citations, quotations, or direction markers.

Requirement: Historical maps/networks shall distinguish birth/death place, residence, journey, meeting, and inferred locations when data supports them.
Acceptance criterion: Unknown/inferred locations are labelled; birth country is not substituted for transmission location.

Requirement: Optional AI shall suggest searches, summaries, candidate links, or draft explanations with citations and explicit acceptance controls.
Acceptance criterion: Unsupported claims can be flagged; private content is not sent externally by default; accepted suggestions retain origin and revision history.

Requirement: Optional semantic retrieval shall label algorithm/model version and separate suggested relevance from confirmed report-family membership.
Acceptance criterion: Suggestions can be accepted/rejected; lexical search remains available independently.
